second_pass_findings.start_name: Edfu (Idfu) city, Aswan Governorate, Egypt — GASCO transmission-line delivery point serving two sugar/paper factories and city households
second_pass_findings.end_name: UNRESOLVED — no source names the specific valve-room/tie-in point where the 37km Edfu spur leaves the GASCO Dahshour–Aswan ('Upper Egypt'/'South Valley') transmission trunk. The only concrete named candidate found — a real, SCADA-controlled gas pressure-reduction & metering station at Kom Ombo (confirmed by Ahram Gate + ElBalad; ElBalad states it supplies Edfu, Nasr al-Nuba, and Kom Ombo) — is DEFINITIVELY RULED OUT: Kom Ombo town (24.467N, 32.950E per Wikipedia) is ~57km straight-line from Edfu (24.9781N, 32.8749E), which is geometrically impossible for a 37km pipeline to span. The true tie-in must be much closer to Edfu than Kom Ombo, but no source names it.
second_pass_findings.corridor_desc: Retry pass upgrades the prior researcher's evidence but does not resolve the tie-in. Two NEW sources this pass: ElBalad (elbalad.news/6735224) profiles a real, named, SCADA-controlled gas pressure-reduction & metering station at Kom Ombo (120M EGP, 2,500 sqm, 20,000 m3/h capacity) and explicitly states it serves >200,000 residents across Edfu, Nasr al-Nuba, and Kom Ombo (25,000 customers, 'Decent Life' initiative); Ahram Gate (gate.ahram.org.eg/News/5306934.aspx) independently confirms the Aswan governor touring this same 'محطة تخفيض ضغط وقياس الغاز الطبيعى' at Kom Ombo. This is a stronger, more specific candidate than the prior pass had (which only had loose 'Kom Ombo is nearby' reasoning) — BUT plugging in verified real-world coordinates (Kom Ombo town 24.467N/32.950E vs Edfu 24.9781N/32.8749E) shows they are ~57km apart in a straight line, which a 37km pipeline cannot span. This definitively rules out Kom Ombo TOWN as the tie-in (previously only flagged as a 'loose bound' at an incorrectly-estimated 15-20km). The station described in ElBalad may be a genuinely real GASCO/Egypt Gas asset that supplies Edfu via LOCAL distribution mains (a separate lower-pressure layer, not necessarily sited in Kom Ombo town itself, and not necessarily the point where the 37km TRANSMISSION spur taps the trunk) — so the actual physical location of whatever station serves this role could be well north of Kom Ombo town, closer to Edfu, but no source pins that location. Recommend leaving at ROUTE_PARTIAL (corridor-only) pending a GASCO network map or tender document naming the tie-in station explicitly; RouteAccuracy capped at 'low'.
